title: Gain and Decibel Converter
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: gain
decibel
voltage gain
power gain
logarithmic scale
amplification and attenuation
electrical engineering
description: Interactive MicroSim that converts between linear gain and decibels for voltage gain (20 log10) and power gain (10 log10) in both directions, shows a 1 V input signal beside the output scaled by the gain, marks the gain on a logarithmic scale from x0.001 to x1000, and lists a quick reference of common values.

educational.topic: Voltage Gain, Power Gain and Decibels
learningObjectives: Calculate conversions between linear gain and decibel notation for voltage and power gains
prerequisites: voltage gain and power gain as ratios

controls.label: Enter as: Linear gain / Decibels
controls.description: Choose which form the slider sets

controls.label: Mode: Voltage gain / Power gain
controls.description: Choose the 20 log10 or 10 log10 formula

controls.label: Reset
controls.description: Restore the default voltage gain of 10

equations: amplitude ratio = sqrt(Ap) for equal resistances
assumptions: Input and output resistances are equal when a power gain is shown as an amplitude ratio

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Calculate by hand first, then check; compare voltage and power formulas for the same number
keyQuestions: Why is the factor 20 for voltage gain but 10 for power gain?
What linear gain corresponds to 0 dB? To a negative number of decibels?
Why do cascaded gains add when they are expressed in decibels?
commonMisconceptions: A negative decibel value means a negative (inverted) gain
assessmentOpportunities: Convert given linear gains to decibels and given decibel values to linear gains for both voltage and power
